title: Investigation of Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy for potential application of biodegradable esophageal stent material

nodes.label: Esophageal stents of 317L stainless steel stay in the body, are far harder than the tissue and invite restenosis and inflammation
A Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy that degrades in the body and alkalinises its surroundings should both disappear on its own and hold back the cells that cause restenosis
Mg-Zn-Y-Nd alloy as the candidate degradable stent metal
Every test runs the alloy against 317L stainless steel as the clinical incumbent, with a blank medium as a third arm in the immersion test
Seed four cell lines that matter clinically (Eca109 cancer, L929 fibroblast, Het-1A epithelial, macrophages) on the metal discs and read AO/EB staining at 4 h, 1 day and 3 days
Both metals cut into 8 mm discs and polished to the same finish
Immersion in Hank's solution at 37 C for up to 30 days, and polarisation in simulated body fluid
Both discs are smooth at the tens-of-nanometre level, the alloy at 57 nm average roughness with parallel polishing grooves against 32 nm for the steel
The alloy is about a quarter as hard as the steel, 54.3 against 198.7 HV
The alloy surface is markedly less wettable, 59.9 deg water contact angle against 28.4 deg for the steel
The alloy corrodes three orders of magnitude faster in simulated body fluid: -1.49 V and 24.93 uA/cm2 against -0.25 V and 0.017 uA/cm2, with an impedance 89% lower
Immersion turns the alloy surface into an open, cracked porous corrosion layer by day 15-30, while the steel surface is unchanged
The measured degradation rate peaks near 0.38 mm/y at day 7 and settles at 0.13-0.16 mm/y by day 22-30, against 0.07 mm/y or less for the steel
Degradation drives the medium from pH 7.4 to about 10 within 22 days, where the blank control drifts down to 7.5
Far fewer cells of all four lines settle on the alloy, and their viable fraction falls with time to 76% at 72 h against about 96% on the steel
The corroding alloy releases OH- and Mg2+ and keeps shedding its surface, so the rising pH and the less wettable, unstable interface stop the pathological cells from anchoring and proliferating

attrs.mechanism_class: alkalinisation plus unstable, poorly wetted interface

nodes.label: As a stent material the alloy does the job in vitro: it degrades steadily in physiological fluid, is far less hard than the steel, and holds back restenosis-related and inflammatory cells

attrs.condition: 30 days in Hank's solution at 37 C; 3 days of cell culture

nodes.label: Mg-Zn-Y-Nd combines degradability, a softer surface and inhibition of the four cell types behind restenosis and inflammation, so it is a candidate esophageal stent material
On every axis measured here the alloy differs from 317L stainless steel in the direction a degradable stent needs

attrs.verdict: favourable on hardness, wettability, degradability and cell inhibition

nodes.label: Everything is in vitro on flat discs: no stent geometry, no radial force or fatigue test, and no in-vivo degradation
The alloy surface carries parallel polishing grooves within a 1 um height range; the steel surface is flat but pocked with isolated pits reaching 2 um deep

nodes.label: The fibroblast, epithelial and macrophage figures repeat the same pattern of fewer cells and lower vital ratios on the alloy
317L stainless steel esophageal stents stay in place permanently and are associated with restenosis and inflammatory response
Magnesium corrodes in chloride media by releasing Mg2+ and OH-, which raises the local pH
In AO/EB staining live cells fluoresce green and dead ones orange-red
Eca109, L929 and Het-1A cells drive restenosis in an esophageal stent and macrophages drive the inflammatory response; the tumour microenvironment is acidic

notes: A screening paper: the whole argument is a two-arm comparison against 317L stainless steel, so DES/variable_sweep carries the material axis and every property node states both arms. The surface branch (roughness -> wettability) and the degradation branch (electrochemistry -> porous corrosion layer -> rate -> pH) meet at the MEC node that explains the cell result. Lost: the alloy composition and microstructure are never characterised in the packet, the fibroblast, epithelial and macrophage figures (F7-F9) were not opened and enter as one text-backed OBS, and the corrosion-rate calculation is not given. Image findings: the steel control drives the medium to pH 6.05 by day 20, nearly two units below the blank control, which the paper never addresses (p8); the alloy's corrosion-rate error bars span most of the decline after day 7, and the electrochemical current implies a faster rate than any immersion point (p9); the viable fraction on the alloy never falls below 76%, so the inhibition is mainly fewer attached cells rather than killing, and the cell counts are never quantified (p10, p11); the roughness panel prints 57.08 +/- 4.65 nm where the text says +/- 4.05 (p2); the steel's profilometry height range is about four times the alloy's because of isolated pits, so the lower average roughness hides deeper defects (p1); the polarisation panel has no abscissa title (p5); the SEM immersion panels carry scale bars with no legible value (p6). Panel section: F3 and F4 are tier B and offered only as whole-figure ids, so the seven-day SEM series and the polarisation curves plus their embedded table are each cited as one panel.

changes: p8: 'a full unit below the blank control' corrected to 'nearly two units below'. Read off F5a at day 20 the blank sits near 7.95 and the steel arm at 6.05. Label, image_note and the graph notes updated; the audit is stronger than the node claimed.

panel_checks.note: the pH panel carries all three arms: the alloy rising 7.4 -> 10.0 and plateauing after about day 22 (p7), the blank peaking near 8.45 around day 4-8 and drifting to about 7.55, and the steel falling to its 6.05 minimum at day 20-21 before recovering to 7.07. Only the size of the steel/blank gap needed correcting.

F3 is offered as a whole-figure id and holds the two Tafel curves plus the table beneath them, which prints -1.49 V / 24.93 uA cm-2 / 8450 ohm cm2 and -0.25 V / 0.017 uA cm-2 / 75190 ohm cm2. The abscissa really carries no title, and the alloy's branches meet near log i = -4.3, i.e. about 50 uA cm-2, roughly twice the tabulated value, as the node says.
the bar chart gives about 88, 83 and 76% on the alloy at 4, 24 and 72 h against about 95.5, 97.5 and 96.5% on the steel, with significance markers at all three times

review.audit_summary: 2 audits (n20 the in-vitro flat-disc scope, p8 the unexplained acidification of the steel control). Both change the support of a spine claim. Three further figure findings that qualify rather than overturn - the corrosion-rate error bars swallowing the post-day-7 decline, the electrochemical current implying a faster rate than any immersion point, and the viable fraction never falling below 76% - are correctly kept inside the image_notes of p9 and p11 rather than spawning audit nodes.
